findings.issue: The generated E2E artefacts are not ignored, and they have now actually been committed: 'git ls-files tests/Wakeel.E2E' lists tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-actual.png, W08-diff.png and W08-diff-percentage.txt as tracked files. These are machine-dependent binaries regenerated on every run (my run already produced a different percentage than the builder's), so they will churn the history on every E2E execution. This is the round-1 low finding the builder correctly refused to fix (outside the package's allowed paths); it now needs supervisor action.
findings.fix: Add a line 'tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/' to .gitignore and run 'git rm --cached tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-actual.png tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-diff.png tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-diff-percentage.txt' so the three generated files stop being tracked.

findings.issue: Line 141, Assert.Equal(percentage.ToString("F4"), File.ReadAllText(percentagePath)), is still close to self-referential: the same test wrote that exact string to that exact path eight lines earlier (line 133), so the assertion can only fail if File.WriteAllText/ReadAllText themselves are broken. It is an improvement over the round-1 tautological Assert.InRange, and the genuinely behavioural assertions in this test (heading text vs Ar.AttentionCenter.Title, the 1366x768 capture size, File.Exists(diffPath)) do carry the test, so this is cosmetic rather than a coverage gap.
findings.fix: Either drop line 141 and keep Assert.True(File.Exists(percentagePath)) plus Assert.True(double.TryParse(File.ReadAllText(percentagePath), NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out _)) — asserting the artefact is a parseable number, which is what a later package will consume — or leave as is; no functional risk either way.

findings.issue: The CDP session created at line 100 (page.Context.NewCDPSessionAsync(page)) is never detached. The finally block clears the device-metrics override but leaves the session attached for the remainder of the fixture's lifetime. Harmless in practice (the app is killed at teardown and the assembly is sequential), but it leaks a CDP attachment that a later package reusing this pattern across many screenshots would multiply.
findings.fix: In the existing finally block, after 'await cdp.SendAsync("Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride");' add 'await cdp.DetachAsync();'.

findings.issue: WaitForPageAsync throws WakeelAppLaunchException(..., processWasKilled: false) at line 157, but InitializeAsync's catch (lines 61-67) immediately calls DisposeAsync, which does kill the process. The diagnostic flag on the propagated exception therefore reports the opposite of what happened. Only a message-accuracy issue — no process is actually leaked (confirmed: tasklist shows zero Wakeel.Desktop.exe and zero Wakeel-owned msedgewebview2.exe after both of my runs).
findings.fix: Either drop the processWasKilled argument from this throw site (it is about page selection, not process launch) by throwing a plain InvalidOperationException, or have InitializeAsync's catch re-wrap with processWasKilled: true after DisposeAsync returns.

findings.issue: ConfigureRemoteDebugging clears WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS unconditionally (line 75). This is the right security default and correctly closes the round-1 inherited-environment hole, but it also silently discards a deliberately-set value in every release build — e.g. a support engineer setting --disable-gpu to work around a rendering fault on a customer machine will find it has no effect, with no log line explaining why. Behavioural decision worth recording rather than a defect.
findings.fix: Optional: before clearing, if Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS") is non-empty, Log.Warning it was ignored — but note ConfigureRemoteDebugging currently runs before ConfigureLogging, so the two calls in OnStartup would have to be swapped, or the warning deferred. Leaving it exactly as is is acceptable.

findings.issue: The W08 diff percentage is not bit-reproducible across machines/sessions: the builder measured 33.3045% twice, my two runs on the same machine measured 33.3047% (artifacts/W08-diff-percentage.txt reads 33.3047). The drift is tiny and harmless now because this package deliberately sets no threshold, but it means the later B1-B8 acceptance packages cannot compare against an exact recorded figure.
findings.fix: No change needed in this package. When B1-B8 introduce thresholds, express them as an upper bound with tolerance (e.g. Assert.True(percentage <= budget)) rather than equality against a recorded value, and consider raising ImageDiff.ChannelDeltaSumThreshold if sub-pixel font rendering proves to be the source.

Two green runs back to back, spec item 5 satisfied.
- MEASURED W08 DIFF PERCENTAGE: 33.30% recorded in test output; tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-diff-percentage.txt reads 33.3047. W08-actual.png and W08-diff.png were both regenerated. (Builder reported 33.3045 — see the low finding on reproducibility.)

ROUND-1 FINDINGS, RE-CHECKED:
- HIGH, start-url origin escape — genuinely fixed, and I verified it independently rather than trusting the builder's PoC. MainWindow.ConfigureStartUrl now rejects empty, no leading '/', path[1]=='/' or '\\', any backslash anywhere, and anything Uri.TryCreate(path, UriKind.Relative) rejects. I wrote a throwaway probe in the scratchpad exercising the resolution BlazorWebView's WebViewManager performs (new Uri(appBaseUri, startPath)) against the escape vectors the guard does NOT explicitly filter — "/\t//evil.com/x", "/\n//evil.com/x", "/\r//evil.com/x", "/ //evil.com/x", "/ //evil.com", "/%2f%2fevil.com/x", "/..//evil.com". Every one resolves back onto the app origin (https://0.0.0.1/...); .NET's Uri does not strip embedded control characters in a way that re-creates a protocol-relative form, and "/..//evil.com" collapses to the same-origin path //evil.com. No residual escape.
- MEDIUM, W08 screenshot DPI — fixed and confirmed. The test asserts Assert.Equal(1366, actualImage.Width) / Assert.Equal(768, actualImage.Height) on the produced PNG and that assertion passed in both of my runs on this 125%-scaled display. The builder's workaround (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride on a fresh CDP session, then Page.captureScreenshot on that session instead of Playwright's ScreenshotAsync) is sound: for a CDP-attached page Playwright re-derives its own viewport state, which is unset, and undoes the override. Worth keeping the explanatory comment at lines 91-99, since the workaround looks gratuitous without it.
- MEDIUM, port collision / stale instance — fixed on both layers. LaunchedWakeelApp.StartAsync probes /json/version before Process.Start and throws a named WakeelAppLaunchException, and WakeelE2eFixture.WaitForPageAsync now matches Uri.AbsolutePath == "/gallery" and reports the observed URL list on timeout.
- LOW, inherited WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS — fixed (unconditional clear before any parsing; see the low finding for the one side effect).
- LOW, process leak on cancellation / no Dispose — fixed: the whole post-Start body is wrapped in catch { KillAsync; Dispose; throw; }, DisposeAsync disposes after killing, and the polling catch now guards with when (!cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) so a genuine cancellation is no longer swallowed.
- LOW, theme not restored — fixed the better way: WakeelE2eFixture captures html[data-theme] once in InitializeAsync and restores exactly that in DisposeAsync, covering every test in the class.
- LOW, tautological Assert.InRange — replaced; see the remaining cosmetic low finding.
- LOW, .gitignore — NOT fixed, and the consequence has now materialised (see finding 1). The builder was right to refuse: the file is outside the package's allowed paths.

SPEC COVERAGE (all five items present):
1. Flags — --remote-debugging-port keeps ushort validation and rejects 0; --window-size=WxH validated (exactly two parts on 'x'/'X', invariant integers, 200..10000) and applied as BlazorView.Width/Height plus SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight, which yields a 1366x768 client area rather than outer bounds (better than the literal spec wording, not a deviation worth flagging); --start-url validated as above, default "/" untouched when absent or malformed. Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable defaults to EnvironmentVariableTarget.Process, so "flags only affect the current process" holds.
2. tests/Wakeel.E2E — builds nothing (WakeelDesktopLocator throws with a build hint if the exe is missing), launches with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --start-url=/gallery, polls http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/version with a 30 s readiness timeout, kills the process and fails with the log tail (WakeelLogs reads ProgramData then LocalAppData with FileShare.ReadWrite|Delete so Serilog's open handle doesn't block it), connects via Playwright.Chromium.ConnectOverCDPAsync, and kills the app in DisposeAsync on every path. All PackageReferences (Microsoft.Playwright 1.62.0, xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, coverlet.collector) resolve from Directory.Packages.props — no new package was added, and System.Drawing comes from UseWindowsForms on the Windows Desktop TFM rather than a NuGet image library. The "no browser download needed for CDP" comment is present in the csproj (lines 29-34).
3. Tests — GalleryOpens asserts html dir=rtl and heading == Ar.Gallery.Title; ThemeToggles asserts data-theme=="dark" AND the computed --w-bg token == #121a1e; W08ScreenshotDiff asserts the heading == Ar.AttentionCenter.Title, pins and asserts a 1366x768 capture, diffs pixel-by-pixel against "design/exports/light/W/W08 — مركز الانتباه.png" (which exists), writes W08-diff.png and W08-diff-percentage.txt into tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/, and only records the percentage with no threshold; AppLaunchTimeoutTests proves the kill-on-timeout path and asserts ProcessWasKilled. These are real behavioural assertions, not tautologies.
4. build/e2e.ps1 — header documents the WebView2 runtime prerequisite, the .NET 10 SDK, and the driver-install fallback via the NuGet-provided playwright.ps1; the script builds Wakeel.Desktop (default Debug) then Wakeel.E2E, then runs dotnet test --no-build, throwing an Arabic message per step. It correctly avoids the rejected --no-dependencies form.
5. Two consecutive green runs plus the measured percentage — done above.

SECURITY SUMMARY: the remote-debugging port is honoured only from this process's own argv and only after ushort validation with 0 rejected; the WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS variable — the sole channel into Chromium switches — is cleared unconditionally first, so nothing inherited can inject switches and the validated integer is the only thing ever written back; --start-url is confined to a same-origin relative route (verified against nine escape vectors). No other Chromium switch is injectable through any code path in this package.
